multiple-profiles.required: agents under at least two profiles at once in real work, with no crossover

all-harnesses.required: Claude, Codex, and Copilot each launched, used, and resumed in the workspace

permission-prompts.required: permission and question prompts raised, seen, answered from the embedded terminal, and cleared

long-running-jobs.required: agents left working for hours across app close/reopen and sleep, found again intact

asl.required: a real asl run supervised from the workspace, including a mailbox question and its reply

overview.required: the overview used in real work to watch and focus several agents

conversation-continuity.required: continue, fork, and handoff from Past Sessions; a conversation resumed after its agent ended

affected-acceptance-rerun.required: each trial defect fixed and its affected acceptance checks rerun, or an explicit statement that the trial found none

rollback.required: the rollback carried out on the operator's installation, or the rehearsals (steps 1 to 4) accepted by the operator with the reason recorded

kitty-fallback.required: a deliberate Kitty launch during the trial with tmux as the default, and pre-transition Kitty sessions finished in place

rehearsal.what: Two runs. (1) The transition and rollback steps 1 to 3 of docs/daily-driver-trial.md, on the candidate build, in the Session 19 world on Seb's MacBook Pro (macOS 27.0.1, arm64): app installed by install-app.sh into a disposable root, an amx outside the app, a real Kitty 0.48.2 of the run's own, stand-in agents that send real hooks. (2) Rollback step 4 in the same kind of world: the earlier release (amx 0.8.0 revision 5645f028f120 built headless on the Studio from a detached worktree; its Agent Mux.app 0.1.0 built and ad-hoc signed on the MacBook from that tree) put over a world the candidate had been used in, with a tmux agent deliberately left running, and then the candidate put back.
rehearsal.observed: (1) 43 passed, 0 failed (second pass; the first pass's 9 failures were driver mistakes, see session-20/driver/README.md). A Kitty session launched before the switch stayed the same process in the same tab, kept reporting to the daemon, and ended in place. With launch_backend = "tmux" a launch with no --backend went to the private server and the app attached one xterm-ghostty terminal to it; --backend kitty still opened a Kitty tab. After the switch was reverted a launch opened a Kitty tab while the tmux agent stayed the same process on the same server. uninstall-app.sh removed the app and left that agent running, answering its terminal, and live to `amx attach --json`; a --backend tmux launch still worked with the app gone. `amx backend stop --yes` ended the server and both agents and left the Kitty session and its hooks untouched; config.toml ended as it began. Teardown: no process left, the MacBook user's own amx, AgentMux directories, Kitty configuration, and app preferences unchanged. (2) 35 passed, 0 failed (second pass; the first pass had 3 failures: two were the driver restarting the daemon without naming Kitty, the third was a checkpoint comparison taken before the candidate daemon had settled and could not be attributed, see session-20/driver/README.md). The earlier amx validated a config that still said launch_backend = "tmux" with a warning (unknown key defaults.launch_backend), also under --strict. With the earlier amx installed, the earlier checkout's install-app.sh run, and the daemon restarted by the earlier amx: amx, daemon and bundled amx all reported revision 5645f028f120; the daemon was ready; a Kitty session launched by the candidate stayed the same process and its hook reached the earlier daemon; the earlier amx launched a Kitty tab whose hooks arrived; it listed the fixture conversation; its app connected (feed: live); it refused --backend and has no attach command. config.toml, the transcript, a handoff file, a worktree file, a plan file and launch_overrides.json were byte for byte unchanged; runtime-sessions.json and runtime-state.json were byte for byte what the candidate's daemon left when it stopped; the installed tmux runtime stayed. The tmux agent was the same process on the same server through the downgrade and answered its terminal; the earlier build did not list it. With the candidate's amx back and the daemon restarted, `amx attach --json` found that session live, the same process, and a Kitty session launched by the earlier build reported to the candidate's daemon. Teardown as in (1); /tmp/amxs20-old removed.
rehearsal.not_shown: `just update` itself was not run in the earlier checkout (its steps were done by hand in the world) and its `amx doctor --strict` was recorded but not judged: the world has no hooks installed, no notifier and no agent-session-loop, so strict doctor reports failures there with either build. Hook files written by the candidate and read by the earlier build were therefore not exercised. The transcript index was not refreshed by the earlier build in the run (its hash did not change), so a refresh across builds was not seen. Nothing was installed into /Applications or on the Studio. No real harness ran. No Developer ID signature or notarization exists. A launch from the app's own menu was not driven. The earlier amx was rebuilt from the same revision and is not byte-identical to the operator's installed binary (sha256:557f00895965 here, e2b3e279d5de installed).
